plan.english: The serpent lay on the mountain. It had shut in the waters, and the earth was dry. The people were thirsty and called upon the god. Then Perkwunos seized the stone and went up there. He slew the serpent. Its two eyes grew dark, and its tongue fell from its mouth. He struck it with the stone and split its head. He freed the waters, and they flowed to the sea. Then the tribe praised the god.

clauses.english: The serpent lay on the mountain.
It had shut in the waters, and the earth was dry.
The people were thirsty and called upon the god.
Then Perkwunos seized the stone and went up there.
He slew the serpent.
Its two eyes grew dark, and its tongue fell from its mouth.
He struck it with the stone and split its head.
He freed the waters, and they flowed to the sea.
Then the tribe praised the god.

plan.english: There was a young man, Of-Good-Fame. He lived in a village with his mother and yoked horses. An ill-minded beast had shut the rivers in a hollow. The livestock had no water. Of-Good-Fame seized a spear and went to the hollow. It saw him and roared. The youth did not tremble; he threw the spear. The spear pierced it, and the beast died. Then the hero broke open the hollow. The waters came forth, and the livestock drank. Great fame came to Of-Good-Fame.

clauses.english: There was a young man, Of-Good-Fame.
He lived in a village with his mother and yoked horses.
An ill-minded beast had shut the rivers in a hollow.
The livestock had no water.
Of-Good-Fame seized a spear and went to the hollow.
It saw him and roared.
The youth did not tremble; he threw the spear.
The spear pierced it, and the beast died.
Then the hero broke open the hollow.
The waters came forth, and the livestock drank.
Great fame came to Of-Good-Fame.

plan.english: Perkwunos, strong god, we praise you. You indeed slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain. You who freed the waters, come to us! You who split the rock, give us your strength! Your fame among men is imperishable. Now mighty is your arm, and bright your eye. Hear our hymn, and be dear to us!

clauses.english: Perkwunos, strong god, we praise you.
You indeed slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain.
You who freed the waters, come to us!
You who split the rock, give us your strength!
Your fame among men is imperishable.
Now mighty is your arm, and bright your eye.
Hear our hymn, and be dear to us!

title: The child asks about the serpent

plan.english: A child asked its grandfather: "Who slew the serpent?" The old man said: "The god of thunder slew it, the strong one. He hit it with a stone from the sky." "Why did he hit it?" "It had shut in the waters, and men were thirsty. Its fangs were long, and its eyes were red. Now the waters flow, and we drink." The child laughed and ran home.

clauses.english: A child asked its grandfather:
"Who slew the serpent?"
The old man said:
"The god of thunder slew it, the strong one.
He hit it with a stone from the sky."
"Why did he hit it?"
"It had shut in the waters, and men were thirsty.
Its fangs were long, and its eyes were red.
Now the waters flow, and we drink."
The child laughed and ran home.

plan.english: When the serpent had died, the currents ran down from the mountain. They filled the wide fields, and the grass grew green. The cows came forth from the stalls and drank the water. The shepherds were glad, and the children played in the water. The women went down to the stream and sang. But its dead body lay on the grass, and the birds ate its flesh.

clauses.english: When the serpent had died, the currents ran down from the mountain.
They filled the wide fields, and the grass grew green.
The cows came forth from the stalls and drank the water.
The shepherds were glad, and the children played in the water.
The women went down to the stream and sang.
But its dead body lay on the grass, and the birds ate its flesh.

plan.english: God, giver of good things, we praise you. Then you set free the waters and the rivers for us. Our cattle drink the water. Our children indeed live and play. Strong one, we sing indeed a hymn to you. Our hearts are glad because of you, good one. Be dear to us, and give us good things!

clauses.english: God, giver of good things, we praise you.
Then you set free the waters and the rivers for us.
Our cattle drink the water.
Our children indeed live and play.
Strong one, we sing indeed a hymn to you.
Our hearts are glad because of you, good one.
Be dear to us, and give us good things!

title: The beast that swallowed the rivers

plan.english: An ill-minded enemy lived under the earth. It came forth and swallowed the currents. The fields dried up, and the sheep were thirsty. The women were hungry, and the old men lay down in grief. The tribe cried out to the gods. The god heard its voice. He yoked swift horses and drove them to the enemy. With the stone he split its body, and the currents flowed out of it. Then the sheep drank, and the tribe rejoiced.

clauses.english: An ill-minded enemy lived under the earth.
It came forth and swallowed the currents.
The fields dried up, and the sheep were thirsty.
The women were hungry, and the old men lay down in grief.
The tribe cried out to the gods.
The god heard its voice.
He yoked swift horses and drove them to the enemy.
With the stone he split its body, and the currents flowed out of it.
Then the sheep drank, and the tribe rejoiced.

plan.english: The worm fell down. Its blood flowed into the sea. Its bones lay in the water. The god stood up there and thundered. Now the water was free. It ran out over the fields, and the sun grew bright. The shepherds saw the dead worm and trembled. Then they were glad and honored him. The shepherds burned its body with fire, and they threw its bones away.

clauses.english: The worm fell down.
Its blood flowed into the sea.
Its bones lay in the water.
The god stood up there and thundered.
Now the water was free.
It ran out over the fields, and the sun grew bright.
The shepherds saw the dead worm and trembled.
Then they were glad and honored him.
The shepherds burned its body with fire, and they threw its bones away.

plan.english: Strong is the god, and strong is his arm. Heavy is his stone, and sharp the spear. His horses are indeed swift. Then he drank the sweet mead and grew strong. He then overpowered the ill-minded beast. No one overcame him in the fight. We sing the might of the strong one.

clauses.english: Strong is the god, and strong is his arm.
Heavy is his stone, and sharp the spear.
His horses are indeed swift.
Then he drank the sweet mead and grew strong.
He then overpowered the ill-minded beast.
No one overcame him in the fight.
We sing the might of the strong one.

plan.english: Father Sky made a stone for his son. The stone was heavy and bright. He gave it to his son and said: "Take this and strike the serpent!" The son took it in hand and climbed a high oak. From there he threw it at the enemy. It hit its head and split it. Then it went back into the hand of the god.

clauses.english: Father Sky made a stone for his son.
The stone was heavy and bright.
He gave it to his son and said:
"Take this and strike the serpent!"
The son took it in hand and climbed a high oak.
From there he threw it at the enemy.
It hit its head and split it.
Then it went back into the hand of the god.

plan.english: The serpent lay around the waters. The gods saw it and trembled before it. They fled up to the sky and hid under the clouds. The god of thunder alone took courage. He said to them: "Do not tremble! I shall kill the serpent." He went there and struck it three times with the stone. Its tail shook, and then it died. The gods came down again and stood around the dead one. They praised him, the one who had dared.

clauses.english: The serpent lay around the waters.
The gods saw it and trembled before it.
They fled up to the sky and hid under the clouds.
The god of thunder alone took courage.
He said to them: "Do not tremble!
I shall kill the serpent."
He went there and struck it three times with the stone.
Its tail shook, and then it died.
The gods came down again and stood around the dead one.
They praised him, the one who had dared.

plan.english: I sing a new hymn to the god. He indeed killed the serpent with the stone. Then he freed the waters for the people of the earth. Hear my song, Perkwunos! Give us livestock and swift horses now! Now guard our homes in the night!

clauses.english: I sing a new hymn to the god.
He indeed killed the serpent with the stone.
Then he freed the waters for the people of the earth.
Hear my song, Perkwunos!
Give us livestock and swift horses now!
Now guard our homes in the night!

plan.english: At night a daughter asked her mother: "Tell me a story." The night was long, and the daughter listened. The mother told the story of the serpent. "A serpent lay in the waters and swallowed them. Men were thirsty, and the cattle died. Then a hero came, Of-Goodly-Fame. He struck the head of the serpent with a stone. The serpent died, and the water came forth." The daughter said: "I am not afraid of it." Her mother laughed and said: "It is dead. Sleep!"

clauses.english: At night a daughter asked her mother: "Tell me a story."
The night was long, and the daughter listened.
The mother told the story of the serpent.
"A serpent lay in the waters and swallowed them.
Men were thirsty, and the cattle died.
Then a hero came, Of-Goodly-Fame.
He struck the head of the serpent with a stone.
The serpent died, and the water came forth."
The daughter said: "I am not afraid of it."
Her mother laughed and said: "It is dead.
Sleep!"

plan.english: Man-Minded went against the enemy. He struck it once with a spear, and it did not die. He struck it twice, and it roared. He struck it three times, and its head split. Its blood was black. Blood ran out of it, and with the blood the waters ran. The streams washed the pebbles, and the trees drank. Man-Minded stood up and lifted his spear. The tribe saw him and praised his famous name.

clauses.english: Man-Minded went against the enemy.
He struck it once with a spear, and it did not die.
He struck it twice, and it roared.
He struck it three times, and its head split.
Its blood was black.
Blood ran out of it, and with the blood the waters ran.
The streams washed the pebbles, and the trees drank.
Man-Minded stood up and lifted his spear.
The tribe saw him and praised his famous name.

plan.english: He struck the serpent, and he freed the waters. He split the rock with the heavy stone. He led the cows out of the hollow rock. The sun grew bright again over the earth. Him we praise now; him we call upon. Let us sing to him, the strong one!

clauses.english: He struck the serpent, and he freed the waters.
He split the rock with the heavy stone.
He led the cows out of the hollow rock.
The sun grew bright again over the earth.
Him we praise now; him we call upon.
Let us sing to him, the strong one!

title: The serpent and the god speak

plan.english: The serpent said to the god: "Who are you? I hold the waters, and no one will take them from me." He answered: "I am Perkwunos. With this stone I shall strike you." It roared and wrapped itself around a tree. Then the god threw the stone, and the serpent fell. The trees shook, and the birds flew up. Its tongue was long, and its teeth were sharp. The god laughed. Its words had been lies.

clauses.english: The serpent said to the god: "Who are you?
I hold the waters, and no one will take them from me."
He answered: "I am Perkwunos.
With this stone I shall strike you."
It roared and wrapped itself around a tree.
Then the god threw the stone, and the serpent fell.
The trees shook, and the birds flew up.
Its tongue was long, and its teeth were sharp.
The god laughed.
Its words had been lies.

plan.english: An enemy drove the cows away and shut them up in a rock. Inside it they cried out with hunger. The god heard their voices. He and Fire went there together. Fire burned the enemy, and the strong one split the rock open with his stone. The enemy fled, but Fire seized him. They came out into the light. The shepherds milked them, and the milk was sweet.

clauses.english: An enemy drove the cows away and shut them up in a rock.
Inside it they cried out with hunger.
The god heard their voices.
He and Fire went there together.
Fire burned the enemy, and the strong one split the rock open with his stone.
The enemy fled, but Fire seized him.
They came out into the light.
The shepherds milked them, and the milk was sweet.

plan.english: Perkwunos, you struck the snake with the stone. Strike our enemies, strong one! Guard our cows and our children! Giver of good things, give us fame indeed! May your stone fly against them! We shall praise you with songs.

clauses.english: Perkwunos, you struck the snake with the stone.
Strike our enemies, strong one!
Guard our cows and our children!
Giver of good things, give us fame indeed!
May your stone fly against them!
We shall praise you with songs.

plan.english: When the god had slain the serpent, the people prepared a feast. They kindled a fire, cooked meat in a cauldron, and poured mead into cups. The young men sang a hymn about the beast. The god came and sat down at the feast. The old men told stories. He drank the mead and was glad. He gave them gifts: cattle and sheep. They said: "Giver of good things, be dear to us!"

clauses.english: When the god had slain the serpent, the people prepared a feast.
They kindled a fire, cooked meat in a cauldron, and poured mead into cups.
The young men sang a hymn about the beast.
The god came and sat down at the feast.
The old men told stories.
He drank the mead and was glad.
He gave them gifts: cattle and sheep.
They said: "Giver of good things, be dear to us!"

plan.english: Two brothers went out against the serpent. The one was afraid; the other took courage. He who took courage stabbed it with a spear. The beast died, and the waters went out from the rock. The brother who had been afraid ran home and said to the people: "My brother slew the beast; praise him!" Their old father laughed with joy. The people honored the brother and gave him gifts: a wheel and a yoke.

clauses.english: Two brothers went out against the serpent.
The one was afraid; the other took courage.
He who took courage stabbed it with a spear.
The beast died, and the waters went out from the rock.
The brother who had been afraid ran home and said to the people:
"My brother slew the beast; praise him!"
Their old father laughed with joy.
The people honored the brother and gave him gifts: a wheel and a yoke.

plan.english: Free waters, flow now! Then the strong one freed you from the snake. You nourish our cattle and our sheep. Waters, mothers, give us good things! Fill our fields indeed with your water! And now you are sweet and bright.

clauses.english: Free waters, flow now!
Then the strong one freed you from the snake.
You nourish our cattle and our sheep.
Waters, mothers, give us good things!
Fill our fields indeed with your water!
And now you are sweet and bright.

plan.english: A son heard the thunder and was afraid. He asked his father: "Why does the sky thunder?" The father said: "Perkwunos strikes the serpent with the stone. It comes back to the waters, and the god strikes it again. Do not fear: afterwards it rains." Then it rained, and the son listened. In the morning the fields were green. He was not afraid, and he slept.

clauses.english: A son heard the thunder and was afraid.
He asked his father: "Why does the sky thunder?"
The father said: "Perkwunos strikes the serpent with the stone.
It comes back to the waters, and the god strikes it again.
Do not fear: afterwards it rains."
Then it rained, and the son listened.
In the morning the fields were green.
He was not afraid, and he slept.

plan.english: Of-True-Fame was a young man. He drank the mead of the gods and became strong. He grew big, and his two arms became heavy. He went to the sea, in which the snake lay. It wrapped itself around him, but the hero got free. He seized its head and cut it off. The sea was red with its blood. He carried the head home, and the tribe rejoiced.

clauses.english: Of-True-Fame was a young man.
He drank the mead of the gods and became strong.
He grew big, and his two arms became heavy.
He went to the sea, in which the snake lay.
It wrapped itself around him, but the hero got free.
He seized its head and cut it off.
The sea was red with its blood.
He carried the head home, and the tribe rejoiced.

plan.english: Imperishable is the fame of the god. Great is his name among the people. Then he slew the serpent, and he freed the waters. Men, sing his famous name! His words are indeed true. Now may his fame be great.

clauses.english: Imperishable is the fame of the god.
Great is his name among the people.
Then he slew the serpent, and he freed the waters.
Men, sing his famous name!
His words are indeed true.
Now may his fame be great.

plan.english: A snake lay beneath the earth, in a deep hollow. There was no light there. It held the currents of the rivers in its teeth. Fame-from-the-Gods went down into the hollow. He carried fire in his hand. It saw the fire and was afraid. It let go of the currents and fled. But the hero followed it and killed it in the dark water. In the hollow lay the bones of many sheep. The rivers flowed up over the fields. Then the hero came up into the sun. His mother saw him and cried out with joy.

clauses.english: A snake lay beneath the earth, in a deep hollow.
There was no light there.
It held the currents of the rivers in its teeth.
Fame-from-the-Gods went down into the hollow.
He carried fire in his hand.
It saw the fire and was afraid.
It let go of the currents and fled.
But the hero followed it and killed it in the dark water.
In the hollow lay the bones of many sheep.
The rivers flowed up over the fields.
Then the hero came up into the sun.
His mother saw him and cried out with joy.

plan.english: The god went out early. He found the serpent on the high mountain. He slew it; he struck it with the stone. The red blood of the serpent ran down from the rocks. The waters were loosed, and the earth drank them. Great fame came to the god, imperishable fame. The young men sang of it at the feast, and the old men listened.

clauses.english: The god went out early.
He found the serpent on the high mountain.
He slew it; he struck it with the stone.
The red blood of the serpent ran down from the rocks.
The waters were loosed, and the earth drank them.
Great fame came to the god, imperishable fame.
The young men sang of it at the feast, and the old men listened.

plan.english: We women now sing to you. God, you slew the snake for us. Our children drink the water. Our livestock gives milk. The sheep gives us wool. Be well now, strong one! May you be good and dear to us!

clauses.english: We women now sing to you.
God, you slew the snake for us.
Our children drink the water.
Our livestock gives milk.
The sheep gives us wool.
Be well now, strong one!
May you be good and dear to us!

plan.english: An old man spoke to the young men. "When the god slew the serpent, I was a child. I remember the thunder and the fire. The sky was black, and the wind roared. The houses trembled, and the trees fell. Then I saw the waters coming down from the rocks. We ran to the river and drank, and our mothers laughed. Tell this story to your children, young ones!"

clauses.english: An old man spoke to the young men.
"When the god slew the serpent, I was a child.
I remember the thunder and the fire.
The sky was black, and the wind roared.
The houses trembled, and the trees fell.
Then I saw the waters coming down from the rocks.
We ran to the river and drank, and our mothers laughed.
Tell this story to your children, young ones!"

plan.english: The snake deceived the god. It lay in the sun and laughed. It said: "I have no water; the waters have gone away." The god went away. But the fields were dry, and the tribe cried out. The god saw the lie and grew angry. He came back and struck it with the heavy stone. He broke its bones, and the water ran out. Its lie did not save it. Its body lay on the pebbles, and the tribe drank the water.

clauses.english: The snake deceived the god.
It lay in the sun and laughed.
It said: "I have no water; the waters have gone away."
The god went away.
But the fields were dry, and the tribe cried out.
The god saw the lie and grew angry.
He came back and struck it with the heavy stone.
He broke its bones, and the water ran out.
Its lie did not save it.
Its body lay on the pebbles, and the tribe drank the water.

plan.english: Who slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain? Perkwunos, the strong one, struck it with the stone. Who indeed freed the waters and the rivers? The giver of good things indeed freed them. His name is famous among the people. Now let us praise him with a hymn!

clauses.english: Who slew the ill-minded serpent on the mountain?
Perkwunos, the strong one, struck it with the stone.
Who indeed freed the waters and the rivers?
The giver of good things indeed freed them.
His name is famous among the people.
Now let us praise him with a hymn!

title: The stone that fell from heaven

plan.english: Father Sky caught sight of the beast in the deep sea. It had swallowed the rain-clouds, and it did not rain on the earth. Then he threw down a great stone. It fell into the sea, and the water boiled. It struck the beast, which lay there in the depths. Its body burst, and the rain-clouds came forth. Then it rained, and the streams became full. The grass grew, and the sheep ate it. Afterwards men found the stone. They set it up in a sacred place and honored it.

clauses.english: Father Sky caught sight of the beast in the deep sea.
It had swallowed the rain-clouds, and it did not rain on the earth.
Then he threw down a great stone.
It fell into the sea, and the water boiled.
It struck the beast, which lay there in the depths.
Its body burst, and the rain-clouds came forth.
Then it rained, and the streams became full.
The grass grew, and the sheep ate it.
Afterwards men found the stone.
They set it up in a sacred place and honored it.

plan.english: The ill-minded one lay in a sea and guarded its water. No one came near it. Then Fire said to the strong god: "I shall dry up the water." Fire blazed, and the sea boiled. The ill-minded one came up out of it. The strong one stood with his stone. He hit it, and it fell dead. Fire burned its body. Fire and the strong one rejoiced together. The tribe sings of those two.

clauses.english: The ill-minded one lay in a sea and guarded its water.
No one came near it.
Then Fire said to the strong god: "I shall dry up the water."
Fire blazed, and the sea boiled.
The ill-minded one came up out of it.
The strong one stood with his stone.
He hit it, and it fell dead.
Fire burned its body.
Fire and the strong one rejoiced together.
The tribe sings of those two.

plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has indeed come. She sees the free streams and the fields. Now the ill-minded one lies on the earth. Praise the god indeed, who killed him! Now sing a song to the strong one! Dawn, bring us good things now!

clauses.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, has indeed come.
She sees the free streams and the fields.
Now the ill-minded one lies on the earth.
Praise the god indeed, who killed him!
Now sing a song to the strong one!
Dawn, bring us good things now!

plan.english: At evening a daughter asked her mother: "Where does the serpent lie now?" She said: "The god bound it with ropes beneath the sea." "Will it come back?" "If it comes, he will strike it again. He is awake, and he protects us. Do not be afraid; rest!" The daughter heard the wind. Above the house the stars shone. The daughter lay down and slept.

clauses.english: At evening a daughter asked her mother: "Where does the serpent lie now?"
She said: "The god bound it with ropes beneath the sea."
"Will it come back?"
"If it comes, he will strike it again.
He is awake, and he protects us.
Do not be afraid; rest!"
The daughter heard the wind.
Above the house the stars shone.
The daughter lay down and slept.

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses drove his horses to the river. A snake came out of the water and wrapped itself around the hero. The horses ran away in fear. The hero called upon the god: "Strong one, free me!" The god heard him and threw a stone from heaven. It hit the worm, and the worm let go of him. Of-Good-Horses got free and pierced it with his spear. His horses came back to their master. Afterwards he gave the god a gift, a white horse.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Horses drove his horses to the river.
A snake came out of the water and wrapped itself around the hero.
The horses ran away in fear.
The hero called upon the god: "Strong one, free me!"
The god heard him and threw a stone from heaven.
It hit the worm, and the worm let go of him.
Of-Good-Horses got free and pierced it with his spear.
His horses came back to their master.
Afterwards he gave the god a gift, a white horse.

plan.english: I am a shepherd, and I praise the god. The sheep drink from the river. A snake indeed held the river; the god set it free. Now guard my sheep, strong one, from the wolf! I shall now give you sweet milk.

clauses.english: I am a shepherd, and I praise the god.
The sheep drink from the river.
A snake indeed held the river; the god set it free.
Now guard my sheep, strong one, from the wolf!
I shall now give you sweet milk.

plan.english: The gods sat together. One said: "Who will slay the serpent?" No one answered; their hearts trembled with fear. Then Perkwunos stood up and said: "I shall go." He yoked his swift horses. The gods chose him and gave him the stone. Father Sky said: "Go, my son, and strike!" He went and struck it, and it died. Then they honored him.

clauses.english: The gods sat together.
One said: "Who will slay the serpent?"
No one answered; their hearts trembled with fear.
Then Perkwunos stood up and said: "I shall go."
He yoked his swift horses.
The gods chose him and gave him the stone.
Father Sky said: "Go, my son, and strike!"
He went and struck it, and it died.
Then they honored him.

plan.english: From inside the rock the waters cried: "Hero, free us!" Of-Goodly-Fame heard their voice and asked: "Who holds you?" "An ill-minded serpent holds us in the rock." He broke it and went in. Inside, the hollow was dark. There he found it lying asleep. He cut off its head, and it did not wake. They came out and said: "You freed us; your fame will be great."

clauses.english: From inside the rock the waters cried: "Hero, free us!"
Of-Goodly-Fame heard their voice and asked: "Who holds you?"
"An ill-minded serpent holds us in the rock."
He broke it and went in.
Inside, the hollow was dark.
There he found it lying asleep.
He cut off its head, and it did not wake.
They came out and said: "You freed us; your fame will be great."

plan.english: Perkwunos, strong one, we call upon you. Come indeed to our feast, you who struck the serpent! Drink indeed the sweet mead that we have poured for you! Give us indeed strength and great fame! Strike the enemies with your stone!

clauses.english: Perkwunos, strong one, we call upon you.
Come indeed to our feast, you who struck the serpent!
Drink indeed the sweet mead that we have poured for you!
Give us indeed strength and great fame!
Strike the enemies with your stone!

plan.english: When the waters had been freed, the people made an oath. They said: "At the new year we shall sing this hymn to the god. We shall give him the first of our cattle." Their sons sing it, and their grandsons sing it. The mothers tell it to their daughters at night. The story lives among the people. The old men sing it at the feast. Hear it, children, and remember the god who freed the waters!

clauses.english: When the waters had been freed, the people made an oath.
They said: "At the new year we shall sing this hymn to the god.
We shall give him the first of our cattle."
Their sons sing it, and their grandsons sing it.
The mothers tell it to their daughters at night.
The story lives among the people.
The old men sing it at the feast.
Hear it, children, and remember the god who freed the waters!
